transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I feel like no matter how hard I plan and work, I’m just not good enough to get ahead. I've just been feeling really stuck and unmotivated lately, and I don't know how to move past it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did it start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

I've been feeling this way for about three years now, starting when I was passed over for a supervisor promotion that I had prepared really hard for. They gave the job to a younger, less-experienced coworker, and around that same time, company budget cuts left me with a much heavier workload.
Since this started, have your feelings been tied mainly to that promotion setback and work changes, or have they spread into many areas of your life even when you’re away from work?

It's definitely spread to other parts of my life, to the point where even my hobbies like neighborhood clean-ups and picking up trash along the river just feel empty and hopeless now. I've also started canceling plans with friends and neighbors so much that they've pretty much stopped asking me to help out or hang around.
Over the past few weeks, have you felt depressed or lost interest and pleasure in things most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, but it's been going on much longer than just a few weeks—it's actually been my baseline for about three years now. Most days feel like there's a gray cloud over everything, where I'm just going through the motions feeling empty and hopeless inside. I've completely lost interest in my hobbies and clean-up projects because nothing feels meaningful anymore.
Have you had any period of at least two months during these three years when you felt back to your usual self and the sadness or loss of interest was mostly gone?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. This heavy, discouraged feeling has been my constant baseline for the entire three years since I was passed over. I haven't had even a month, let alone two, where I felt back to my usual self.
During this time, have you also had symptoms like major changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, or thoughts of death or suicide?

I definitely struggle with sleep, often lying awake for hours worrying, and my brain feels stuck in mud when I try to concentrate or read simple emails. I constantly feel worthless and like I'm just not good enough to get ahead, but I haven't had any changes in my appetite or thoughts of suicide.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where your depression got much worse and you had several symptoms like very low energy, major sleep or appetite changes, or feeling unable to function at work or at home?

No, it hasn't really come in sudden, severe spikes like that. Instead, this low mood, poor sleep, and just doing the bare minimum at work and with friends has been a constant, steady weight for the last three years. It has just been my normal, everyday baseline ever since I missed out on that promotion.
Have you ever had a period of at least a few days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or became more confident and active than normal?
No, I've never experienced anything like that with high energy or feeling extra confident. My mood has just been consistently low, flat, and discouraged over the past few years.

Do you feel your symptoms are mainly a response to the promotion setback and work stress, or have they become a long-lasting part of your mood even when things are going relatively well? Has this low mood been present most days for at least two years without a break of two months or more?

It definitely started with the promotion setback and work stress, but it has since become my constant baseline even when things are going fine. This heavy, discouraged mood has been with me almost every single day for the past three years without any break at all.

Did your symptoms begin within about 3 months of the promotion setback and work stress, and have they mostly stayed tied to that stressor? Or do they feel more like a persistent low mood that is not just a reaction to the event?

Yes, it started right around the time I was passed over for the promotion three years ago, but it has evolved into a constant, heavy baseline rather than just a temporary reaction to that setback. This gray cloud has been with me almost every single day since then, and it really just feels like my new normal now.

Have there been any periods during the last three years when your mood and motivation improved enough that you felt mostly like yourself again for at least a couple of months? Or has the low mood been present most days regardless of what was happening at work or in your life?

No, I haven't had any periods of relief like that at all. This heavy, discouraged mood has been my constant baseline pretty much every day for the past three years, without any breaks of a couple of months where I felt like my old self. It's just been there constantly, regardless of what is happening in my life.

Did your low mood and loss of interest start only as a reaction to the promotion setback and work stress, or have you had a depressed mood for most days for at least two years even when the stressor was not on your mind?

This low, discouraged feeling has been my constant baseline for about three years now, ever since I was passed over for that promotion. It is there most days like a constant gray cloud and an empty feeling, even when I'm not actively thinking about work or the promotion.

Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the promotion setback and work stress, and do they feel mainly tied to that stressor? Or have they continued as a persistent low mood even when the stressor is not on your mind?

Yes, it started right around the time of the promotion setback about three years ago. But it doesn't feel tied to just that anymore—it has become a constant gray cloud that is with me every day, even when I'm not thinking about work or the promotion at all.

Before this promotion setback, had you ever had a long-lasting low mood, low self-esteem, or feeling like you were not good enough for most days for at least two years? Or did these feelings start only after that event and have stayed constant since then?

No, I didn't feel like this before that setback at all. Back then, I was actually highly motivated, actively planning my career and taking classes without any of this heavy, discouraged feeling. These feelings of low mood and low self-esteem only started after I was passed over three years ago and have been constant ever since.
Have you had any periods during the last three years when you felt mostly back to your usual self for at least two months, or has this low mood been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any breaks at all. This heavy, discouraged feeling has been my constant baseline nearly every single day for the entire three years since I was passed over. I haven't had any periods where I felt back to my usual self.

Have you also had a long-standing pattern of feeling very sensitive to criticism or rejection, or being especially pessimistic and self-critical for most of your life, even before this promotion setback?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought much about whether I was overly sensitive or pessimistic before all of that happened. I just know that things have felt completely different and much heavier since I missed out on that promotion.

Before the promotion setback, did you often feel this kind of low self-esteem, pessimism, or sensitivity to criticism for most of your life? Or did those feelings only start after the setback and work stress?

I've always had some underlying self-doubt and a feeling that I wasn't quite good enough, so when they passed me over, it kind of confirmed what I already thought about myself. However, this heavy, daily discouragement and feeling completely stuck only became my continuous baseline after that setback and the work stress started three years ago.
Before the promotion setback, did you already have a depressed or low self-esteem mood for most days for at least two years, or did those feelings only start after that event?

No, I didn't have a depressed mood most days before that. While I've always had some underlying self-doubt, the heavy, constant depressed mood and feeling of being stuck really only became my daily baseline after I was passed over for the promotion three years ago. It definitely started after that event rather than being present for years before it.
Before the promotion setback, did you already have a depressed mood, low self-esteem, or feeling “not good enough” most days for at least two years, or did those feelings only start after that event?

No, I didn't feel that way most days before the setback. While I might have had some underlying self-doubt, I was still actively planning and trying to get ahead back then. It was only after being passed over three years ago that this daily gray cloud and the deep feeling of not being good enough became my constant baseline.

When you think about the promotion setback and work stress, do your symptoms still feel directly tied to that stressor, or have they become a persistent depressed mood and loss of interest that continues even when the stressor is not on your mind?

While it originally started after being passed over three years ago, it has now become my constant, daily baseline. This gray cloud and empty feeling persist even when I'm not thinking about work, affecting my hobbies like neighborhood cleanups and financial planning. I just feel completely stuck regardless of the situation.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks during these three years when your mood got clearly worse and you had several additional symptoms like major changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or functioning? Or has it been a steady low mood without a distinct severe episode?

No, it hasn't really come in sudden, severe spikes like that. It has just been a steady, continuous low mood and a constant baseline of feeling discouraged and empty for the entire three years. It's just a flat, heavy weight that doesn't really lift or get much worse.

Before this started, did you ever have a period of at least 2 years where you felt depressed or low most days, even without a major stressor? Or did the low mood begin only after the promotion setback and stay continuous since then?

No, I never had any long periods of feeling depressed or low before that. Back then, I was actually highly motivated, active, and focused on planning my career and my hobbies. This continuous, heavy feeling only started after I was passed over for the promotion three years ago and has been constant ever since.

Do you feel your low mood and loss of interest are still mainly a direct reaction to the promotion setback and work stress, or have they become a persistent depressed mood that continues even when those stressors are not on your mind?

It definitely started with the promotion setback and work stress three years ago, but it has now become a constant, heavy baseline. This gray cloud persists almost every day, even when I'm not actively thinking about work or those specific stressors.

Before the promotion setback, did you already have a long-standing pattern of low mood, low self-esteem, or feeling 'not good enough' for most days for at least two years? Or did those feelings only start after that event and stay constant since then?

I've had some underlying self-doubt for a long time, which that rejection seemed to confirm, but I didn't have a daily low mood before then. The continuous gray cloud and loss of motivation definitely solidified and became my constant baseline only after I was passed over three years ago. Before that, I was still able to stay motivated and keep planning for my future.

Before the promotion setback, did you often feel low, pessimistic, or not good enough for most of your life, even as a teenager or young adult? Or did those feelings only become a constant problem after that event?

Before that setback, I had normal ups and downs, but I was highly motivated, taking classes, and actively planning my career. This constant, heavy, and discouraged feeling only became my baseline after I was passed over for the promotion about three years ago. Since then, the feeling of not being good enough has just been a constant cloud over everything.

Before this promotion setback, had you already been feeling down, self-critical, or "not good enough" most days for at least two years? Or did those feelings only begin after the setback and work stress started?

I've had some underlying self-doubt and feelings of not being good enough for a long time, which that setback kind of confirmed. But the actual constant, heavy, and discouraged mood only became my daily baseline after I was passed over for the promotion about three years ago. Before that, it wasn't a daily cloud over my life like it is now.

Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during the last three years when your mood and interest improved back to your usual self, or has the low mood been present most days without any such break?

No, I haven't had any breaks or periods where I felt back to normal. This heavy, discouraged feeling has just been my constant baseline ever since I was passed over for that promotion three years ago, without any relief.

No, I didn't feel that way before the setback. This low mood and discouraged feeling only started after I was passed over for the promotion about three years ago, and it has been my constant baseline ever since.

Yes, my feelings started right around the time I was passed over for the promotion about three years ago. While it might have started as a reaction to that setback, it has since become a constant, persistent gray cloud and my new baseline mood. I feel this empty, hopeless mood even when I'm not thinking about work at all, like when I'm just going through my daily routines or trying to participate in my river clean-up projects.
